item: a Stop shuts a live mailbox pull's socket down; mailbox reads and writes time out after 60 s
summary: R640 reads the switch before every mailbox command, which cannot help a pull already blocked inside one. The live IMAP/POP3 socket is now registered the moment it exists, before the greeting is read, and activate_kill_switch shuts it down at the TCP level (no LOGOUT/QUIT, no TLS close record), as R638 closes the HTTP pools, so a pull blocked on a stalled server ends at the Stop and keeps what it fetched. imaplib and poplib get a 60 s timeout (MAILBOX_TIMEOUT_S). SECURITY.md states the window between the switch read and the write, in which at most one command can still go out. Release line: turning airplane mode on now ends a newsletter mailbox pull at once even if the mail server has stopped answering, and a silent mail server no longer holds a pull for more than a minute.
